2.2.1 Since the upper tuyeres are one metre above the lower tuyeres which would normally be the josition of the conventional tuyeres, the total coke bed height should be increased by about one netre above that while operating with one row of tuyeres. 2.2.2 The normal size of the tuyeres generally has little effect on cupola~performance, the uyeres in the upper row may either be of the same size as the existing tuyeres which will form the ower row on conversion, or alternately, the tuyeres size may be reduced so as to have the same otal tuyere area as before. Each tuyere in both the rows of tuyeres should be fitted with an insulatng valve, which when closed, will prevent cup~ola gases entering the wind belt during long shut lown periods. 2.2.3 The two see Fig. 1 ). rows of tuyeres are spaced between 760 to 915 mm (30 and 36" ) apart

2.2.4 An air inlet pipe shall be arranged tangentially to both the wind belts. Fan type blower may It is recommended that a single fan or blower be used to supply air to both rows of be used. uyeres. However, if so required, a separate fan may be installed for the supply of air to each row )f tuyeres. If a separate fan is installed for each row of tuyeres, it is necessary to ensure that idequate precautions are taken to prevent air being blown to only one row of tuyeres, causing :upola gases to be discharged into the tuyeres and wind belt system of the other row of tuyeres, :reating a definite explosion risk. It is for this reason that a single fan of adequate capacity is ,ecommended. If two fans are used, the starters should be interconnected so that it is impossible `or one fan to operate without the other. If fan type blowers of sufficient high discharge pressure are :u-polas, then a centrifugal positive displacement blower may be used. speed positive displacement blower, control of the blast rate must be ralve in a bleed-off duct in each of the blast mains between the blower .he excess air to be exhausted to atmosphere. not available for larger dia However, when using single accomplished by means of a and the wind belts to enable

2.3 It is essential that a divided blast cupola is fitted with two rows of tuyeres such that each ro\l\r of tuyeres receives an approximately equal quantity of air. ~For this purpose, two air measuremeni and control instruments are inserted in the mains supplying the blast to the cupola. The installation of simple metering equipment consisting of 8n orifice plate and flow indicator for each main is essential. Control of air distribution to each row of tuyeres may be done by manual operation oi the isolating valves. However, as changes in the resistance to flow can cause a variation in the proportions of air supplied to each row of tuyeres, it is imperative that the cupola operator shoulc constantly check and control the flow of blast to each row of tuyeres as this operation wil! essentially remain manual. Where a standby fan is available, the outlets from both the fans should be fed into a common blast main before dividing the blast to separate wind belts, as shown in Fig. 28. Divided blast cupola design shall always incorporate normal safety features to guard against possible explosions occurring as a result of cupola gases entering the tuyeres, wind belt and blast mains during blastoff periods. When changing to two rows of tuyeres, explosion doors, check valves, tuyere cover, flap and tuyeres elbow valves should be installed in such a way as to safeguard both the blast mains and both the windbelts involved. In both cases, it is recommended that the isolating valves in the upper and lower blast mains of each cupola shall have a common linkage, thereby allowing the air blast to the upper and lower tuyeres to be shut off or applied simultaneously. 2.5 The divided blast cupola improves the efficiency of the cu~pola operation and (a) a higher metal tapping temperature and a higher carbon pick up can be obtained for a given coke consumption, or (b) the coke consumption can be appreciably reduced and -melting capacity increased for a given temperature. 2.6 While constructing the shell of the cupola, the brick retaining rings shall be riveted around the inside of the shell below and above the chargin~g door to help in keeping the brick lining in place. 2.6.1 The size of the brick retaining rings below the charging door shall be at a distance of 1 200 mm above the upper tuyeres and subsequently after every 1 200 mm height. The size of brick retaining rings above the charging door shall be 100 mm wide and 16 to 25 mm thick according to the size of cupola and these rings shall be placed 1200 mm apart. 2.7 In building the clear of the cupola For larger cupola between the lining 2.8 To protect lining for cupola diameters up to 750 mm, the fire bricks shall be about 12 mm shell and this space shall be filled with sand or genister as the work proceeds. furnaces, split bricks of thickness ranging from 50 to 75 mm shall be used in and the sand filling. cast iron -blocks shall above the charging be provided just below between the charging door, to

IS : 12272 - 1987 EXPLANATORY NOTE
based on the development of

This standard on divided blast cupola has been formulated, this type of cupola by B. C. I. R. A,, United Kingdom.

This standard describes the design of divided blast cupolas and modification to the existing cupolas which can be carried out for coversion to divided blast operation. The purpose of this standard is to guide the designers of cupolas and to assist the-foundries to make the necessary alterations to their existing cupola installations to derive the advantages of divided blast operation. These are as follows: a) Reduction b) Increase in coke consumption in melting of about 20 percent charge output for same tapping temperature, i-n tapping without rate with same coke consumption, coke consumption rates can give an increase up to

c) Divided blast without reduced temperature of up to 50�C and d) The reduced coke charge enables increasing the normal blast rate.

to be, increased

10 percent

Divided blast cupolas are not suitable for melts hours as the saving in charge coke may not compensate required.
